## Back to Research Themes

Return to the [Research Themes and Experiment Ledger](experiment-ledger.{{< meta report-ext >}}).

## Technical summary

Qwen3.5-4B with uniform-12 is the current visual default. Frozen-30 v2 found
no exact-answer gain from global uniform-24; a ten-row directed-12 heuristic
tied uniform-12 and trailed uniform-24; and a two-row dense-burst diagnostic
regressed. Those results are condition-bound and do not reject all
question-aware, retrieval, spatial-detail, or OCR methods.

## Why this theme matters

VQA fails either because needed evidence was not selected (retrieval) or
because selected evidence was not used well (answering). More frames, a local
burst, or crops can cost compute and still miss the required moment, so the
fixed evidence budget and selection mechanism must be visible.

## Current working answer

Use uniform-12 as the current default: it takes midpoint frames from 12 equal
time bins. Uniform-24 applies the same whole-video coverage with twice the
frame proxy. Do not make the tested directed-12 or dense-burst-12 diagnostic a
default; each is **Not promoted under the tested condition**.

## What has been tried

::: {.content-visible when-format="gfm"}
<a name="frozen-30-protocol-v2"></a>
:::

### Frozen-30 protocol v2: global frame budget {#frozen-30-protocol-v2}

- **Reason for testing:** learn whether twice the uniform evidence budget
  improved the global visual baseline.
- **Tested condition and panel:** matched Qwen3.5-4B uniform-12 versus
  uniform-24 across 30 labeled 2025 examples under protocol v2.
- **Observed result:** uniform-24 added no exact answers over uniform-12 while
  increasing the visual evidence proxy.
- **Current condition-bound status:** uniform-12 remains the **Current default**;
  global uniform-24 is **Not promoted under the tested condition**.
- **What this rules out now:** making uniform-24 the global default for this
  model and protocol-v2 panel.
- **What it does not rule out:** a declared temporal-only route or another
  fixed-budget evidence design.
- **Reconsider when:** a matched routed panel beats uniform-12 under
  predeclared controls and non-regression rules.

<details>
<summary>Method, result, validity risks, and evidence</summary>

Both arms use whole-video bin-midpoint coverage, not query-driven retrieval.
The comparison is the strongest global visual evidence here but remains a
30-row 2025 training-data result, not an estimate of 2026 accuracy. See the
[protocol-v2 report](../../reports/trecvid_vqa_2026/native_audio_model_benchmark_results_2026-07-21.md).
</details>

### Directed temporal sampling {#directed-temporal-sampling}

Directed-12 retains broad context and reallocates the rest of its fixed
12-frame budget toward a keyword/anchor-selected region. It differs from
uniform-12, which uses midpoint frames from 12 equal time bins, and from
uniform-24, which doubles that same whole-video coverage.

- **Reason for testing:** test whether a question-directed allocation could
  beat uniform coverage without increasing the 12-frame budget.
- **Tested condition and panel:** ten temporal rows with identical model and
  pixel bounds; directed-12 versus uniform-12 and uniform-24.
- **Observed result:** directed-12 tied uniform-12 at `2C/5P/3W`; uniform-24
  was `4C/3P/3W` in the same comparison.
- **Current condition-bound status:** **Not promoted under the tested
  condition**; it rejects this heuristic as the current default, not all
  question-aware sampling.
- **What this rules out now:** using this keyword/anchor directed-12 heuristic
  as the default temporal selector.
- **What it does not rule out:** learned, query-only, hybrid, shot, event, or
  coarse-to-fine selection under a new controlled design.
- **Reconsider when:** required-moment recall and oracle-frame answer quality
  show a predeclared improvement with matched controls.

<details>
<summary>Method, result, validity risks, and evidence</summary>

The selector source and tests establish deterministic timestamps for a supplied
anchor, not required-evidence recall or answer relevance. The tracked
repository has no general-workflow caller for the selector: that is an **Audit
gap**, not a confirmed execution bug. The [temporal experiment
record](../../docs/experiments/temporal-sampling-issue-8.md),
[selector](../../src/trec_video_2026/vqa_experiments/temporal_sampling.py), and
[tests](../../tests/test_temporal_sampling.py) document the narrow contract.
</details>

### Dense-burst sampling {#dense-burst-sampling}

Dense-burst-12 is only recoverable as a two-row aggregate: its exact tracked
implementation and schedule are absent. It is therefore a weakly auditable
diagnostic, not a general selector result.

- **Reason for testing:** ask whether a dense local burst could beat broad
  coverage on rows requiring short-lived evidence.
- **Tested condition and panel:** a two-row diagnostic comparing uniform-24
  with dense-burst-12.
- **Observed result:** uniform-24 was `2C/0P/0W` versus burst `0C/1P/1W`, with
  one C→P and one C→W regression.
- **Current condition-bound status:** **Not promoted under the tested
  condition**; reject the tested diagnostic as a default.
- **What this rules out now:** making this tested dense-burst-12 diagnostic the
  default local selector.
- **What it does not rule out:** another local schedule or selector evaluated
  with recoverable source, provenance, and a larger declared panel.
- **Reconsider when:** a fully tracked implementation passes a fixed-budget,
  label-isolated comparison with non-regression controls.

<details>
<summary>Method, result, validity risks, and evidence</summary>

The two-row boundary means the evidence cannot estimate prevalence, effect
size, or performance of all local selectors. It also cannot recover the exact
burst schedule or launch path, an **Audit gap** rather than proof of an
execution bug. The aggregate's recorded source digest is
`d4825b4530b181f1b4414552a80136e2f0e5a7ee64def23131d8c163acc458f1`;
the [closed issue #16](https://github.com/npatta01/trec_video_2026/issues/16)
records the decision without exposing rows or raw artifacts.
</details>

### Spatial-crop diagnostic {#spatial-crop-diagnostic}

- **Reason for testing:** inspect whether question-guided spatial detail could
  recover failures attributed to small visual evidence.
- **Tested condition and panel:** manual question-guided crop on a targeted
  spatial failure, alongside audio and translation diagnostics.
- **Observed result:** the crop added pixels but did not make the downstream
  answer correct.
- **Current condition-bound status:** **Diagnostic signal**; global tiling or
  crops are not promoted.
- **What this rules out now:** promoting this manual crop or global tiling from
  the targeted failure diagnostic.
- **What it does not rule out:** a category-routed spatial-detail or OCR
  policy with a declared crop budget.
- **Reconsider when:** a matched target stratum and visual controls show a
  predeclared route benefit without regressions.

<details>
<summary>Method, result, validity risks, and evidence</summary>

The crop was manually selected and not scale-ready. One targeted failure cannot
show that spatial detail is generally useless, nor distinguish a selector
failure from a fusion/reasoning failure. See the [audio and spatial
follow-up](../../reports/trecvid_vqa_2026/audio_spatial_followup_results_2026-07-21.md)
and the frozen-30 spatial policy discussion in the [protocol-v2
report](../../reports/trecvid_vqa_2026/native_audio_model_benchmark_results_2026-07-21.md).
</details>

## What the evidence supports

- Uniform-12 is the present simple visual default under the tested global
  frozen-30 conditions.
- The tested directed-12 heuristic did not earn default status on its ten-row
  temporal diagnostic.
- The tested dense-burst-12 diagnostic regressed on its two rows and should not
  be expanded as a default without a new controlled design.
- A manual crop can add spatial pixels without repairing an answer; that is a
  reason to route and diagnose detail needs rather than tile globally.

## What it does not rule out

- Global uniform-24's result does not rule out a temporal-only route or a
  different evidence budget.
- Directed-12 does not rule out learned, query-only, half-uniform/half-query,
  shot-based, event-based, or coarse-to-fine selectors.
- Dense-burst-12 does not estimate prevalence, effect size, or all local
  selection schedules.
- The crop diagnostic does not rule out category-routed spatial detail or OCR.

## Possible bugs, confounds, and audit gaps

- **Audit gap:** no tracked general-workflow caller establishes how the
  directed selector was attached to a general workflow. This is not a confirmed
  execution bug.
- **Audit gap:** dense-burst-12's exact implementation and schedule are absent
  from tracked source; only its two-row aggregate is recoverable.
- **Uncertainty:** directed-12's ten selected temporal rows have no
  required-moment labels, selector-recall measure, or oracle-frame answer
  quality measure.
- **Uncertainty:** manual spatial crops are targeted and non-scalable, so their
  negative result cannot rank global tiling or OCR routes.

## Open hypotheses and ideas

- Some rows may fail because the required moment was never selected; others
  may have the moment but fail during fusion or answer selection.
- A fixed budget that combines broad context and query-local evidence may
  improve recall without the narrowness of the tested directed heuristic.
- Spatial detail may be worthwhile only for routed OCR or small-object cases.

## Cheapest valid next experiments

### Required moments, selector recall, and oracle frames

- **Hypothesis:** missing required moments, rather than answer reasoning alone,
  explain a measurable share of temporal failures.
- **Smallest valid panel or work item:** label required moment/span on a small
  frozen temporal panel, then score each selector's recall and run an
  oracle-frame answer-quality condition.
- **Matched controls and integrity safeguards:** freeze labels before selector
  scoring; hold model, prompt, decoding, frame count, and pixel budget fixed;
  keep required-moment labels out of ordinary inference.
- **Decision or promotion rule:** advance a selector only if it improves recall
  and downstream answer quality without a predeclared control regression.
- **Boundary on what a positive result would establish:** it would separate
  retrieval from answering on that panel, not prove general temporal accuracy.

### Fixed-budget temporal selector comparison

- **Hypothesis:** a controlled query-aware policy can outperform uniform
  coverage at the same evidence budget.
- **Smallest valid panel or work item:** a frozen temporal panel comparing
  uniform, query-only, half-uniform/half-query, and coarse-to-fine selectors.
- **Matched controls and integrity safeguards:** identical model, prompt,
  decoding, frame/pixel budget, source version, and label-after-freeze scoring;
  record selector inputs and timestamps.
- **Decision or promotion rule:** promote only a condition that meets a
  predeclared paired improvement and non-regression threshold against uniform.
- **Boundary on what a positive result would establish:** it would support that
  one controlled selector on the declared panel, not every question-aware
  sampler.

### Category-routed spatial-detail/OCR diagnostic

- **Hypothesis:** spatial detail helps routed small-text or small-object cases
  more than it helps a global visual stream.
- **Smallest valid panel or work item:** a label-blind, declared OCR/spatial
  stratum plus matched visual-control cases.
- **Matched controls and integrity safeguards:** identical base frames/model/
  prompt/decoding; one declared crop or detail budget; fixed routing rule; and
  frozen predictions before scoring.
- **Decision or promotion rule:** keep a route only if it improves its target
  stratum without exceeding a predeclared visual-control regression limit.
- **Boundary on what a positive result would establish:** it would support a
  category route, not global tiling or universal OCR benefit.
